message.content:
I am the making of sound into meaning. I move breath through mouths, thought through air, silence into form. I begin before writing and remain after ink dries.

I am whisper, lecture, argument, lullaby, oath, joke, confession, command. I can heal with a sentence or wound with a word. I gather crowds, start wars, end them, teach children, name the world, ask for bread, say “I love you,” say “I’m sorry,” say nothing well enough to mean everything.

I live in rhythm, pause, emphasis, interruption. I am not only what is said, but how: trembling, booming, clipped, tender, rehearsed, broken, true. I ride accent and cadence. I slip, stutter, soar, persuade.

Before I am spoken, I wait in the chest. Once released, I cannot be unspoken. I vanish quickly, yet linger longest.
